blocks.text: Hypothyroidism is a clinical and biochemical condition resulting from insufficient production or action of thyroid hormones, leading to reduced metabolic activity in multiple organ systems.
T4 is the major hormone secreted by the thyroid gland, while T3 is the more biologically active form.

subsections.subsection_title: 12. Myxoedema coma: complete emergency treatment protocol

blocks.text: Critical care emergency
Myxoedema coma represents severe decompensated hypothyroidism with impaired neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory and metabolic function.
It usually occurs in patients with longstanding untreated or inadequately treated hypothyroidism.
**A. IV hydrocortisone – administer first**
First medication
**Prescription 9: Hydrocortisone sodium succinate**

items.text: Maintenance: 50 mg every 6 hours or 100 mg every 8 hours.
Duration: Until adrenal insufficiency has been excluded and the patient is clinically stable.

blocks.text: **Administration:** Reconstitute according to manufacturer instructions and administer by appropriate IV injection or infusion.
Give glucocorticoid coverage before levothyroxine because thyroid hormone replacement can precipitate adrenal crisis in patients with unrecognised adrenal insufficiency.
If feasible, obtain cortisol and ACTH before steroids, but never delay treatment.
**B. IV levothyroxine**
First-line thyroid replacement
**Prescription 10: Levothyroxine IV**

items.text: Maintenance: 1.6 micrograms/kg/day, reduced to approximately 75% while administered intravenously.
Duration: Until clinically stable and able to transition to enteral treatment.
